title: Compute: virtual machines, images and autoscaling

videos.script: You have probably rented a server before without asking what, exactly, you were renting. In the cloud a server is an instance. {{host}} It is a slice of a machine somebody else runs, and you pay for it by the second. This lesson starts there. It reads an instance type the way the price list writes it, and turns an hourly price into a month you can put in a budget. {{sheet}} Then it takes a launch apart. An instance needs an image, a type, a place in a network and a firewall. It needs a key and a disk. It can also carry instructions for its first boot, and you will read a real set and check it on a laptop. {{config}} After that come the prices you can negotiate. A year of commitment buys a discount, and spare capacity buys a bigger one, with a catch. {{prices}} The second half is about many machines instead of one. An autoscaling group keeps a count of healthy instances and replaces the ones that fail. It adds machines when the load rises, but always a few minutes late. {{group}} All of that works only if an instance can be thrown away without losing anything. The last section says where everything else has to live. {{state}} There is no cloud account in this course. Every price comes from the public list, and every command ran without credentials.
